questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Availability to go with partner.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Not easy, but not completely horrible. 
they sent alot of information via E-mail before even starting so it was ok. but navigating a new system is never easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: not much.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: yeah - we used Airbnb. I bit more expensive, but really easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transport is pretty good. but i would live close to the campus (under 25min on foot) everything happens close to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Alot of our classmates were not satisfied with university housing or similar private offerings.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Really weird - we had to sign up to last years classes, so they could get procceced only to choose new ones really close to semester start.
This gave problems with approval.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Really weird - we had to sign up to last years classes, so they could get procceced only to choose new ones really close to semester start.
This gave problems with approval.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you could write an email - but mine was never responded to.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful - but it was first come, first serve - so be ready when registration begins.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: be ready when registration begins.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
it was kind of a joke to be honest. 
Most was attendance based.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
unserious - mostly students doing presentations written by AI. 
and since we were mostly graded based on those - there was not much reason to listen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: again mostly student presentations and while thats similar - that was the only thing we were graded on - so you prepared for that presentation and then you really didn't have to do much more during the rest of the year.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Law Classroom
International Company Law and Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A)
Applied Criminology
International, European and national aviation and space law
Membership in the EU and the Problems of Democracy and Human Rights Protection (internet course)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International Company Law and Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A)
this class was a bit more serious and the teacher was good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: nothing really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
It is cheaper than in Denmark - but not as much as we were told. 
inflation is also present in Poland. 
though some things are basicly free - grocceries common in Poland like potatos is really really cheap. 
while more "exotic food" is more expensive than Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
alot of Erasmus event. 
Polish your polish bar event, movie nights, parties etc. 
also you could sign up for all kinds of sport.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: choose some kind of Erasmus housing - people made friends within those housing units. it was difficult to be a part of that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to different Polish cities. 
Its alot cheaper than Warsaw, and also beautiful - you will be surprised of the cultural heritage.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Poles are quite closed off - much easier with other exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the rudeness. Poles are generally a lot more harsh. its just the culture, and its completely fine when you get used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Cheap public transport for university students.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
before buying student tickets get your UW student card first - all other student cards are not valid. 
If you are not extremely social, find Erasmus housing. 
Learn Polish while you are there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: learning to navigate being abroad, and learning how institutions work differently.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Getting the exam date and exam form.
so frustrating...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
